# aki's Discord Tools

The tools, the API reference and the licence in one file. Generated from the documentation sources
and the endpoint registry, so it matches the site.

Site: https://distools.itzdanti.dev
API base: https://distools.itzdanti.dev/api/v1
Client module: https://distools.itzdanti.dev/api/v1/client.js
Repository: https://github.com/itzdanti/distools

---


# Tools

Every tool is at https://distools.itzdanti.dev/tool/<slug> and runs entirely in the browser. Only tools that
fetch something from Discord make a network request, and those send nothing but the identifier
you typed.

Webhooks are the exception worth naming: the webhook tools post directly to Discord from your
browser, because a webhook URL is a password and must not touch a third party.

---

# API reference

53 endpoints across 10 groups.

Every endpoint accepts GET with query parameters and POST with a JSON body. Both run in your own
runtime through the client module, or over HTTP against a self-hosted copy of the handler. GitHub
Pages only serves files, so a parameterised call to it returns the HTML shell.

Three ways to call it:

1. Open the URL in a browser. The site computes and renders the answer.
2. Import the client module. This is the supported way to call it from code.
3. curl the pre-baked discovery JSON, which are real files.

A plain fetch() of a parameterised endpoint from another origin returns the HTML shell, because
there is no server to run the handler. That is a property of static hosting, not a defect.

### Text

- GET /api/v1/text/fancy
  id: text.fancy
  Convert text to a fancy Unicode style
      - text (required): Text to convert.
      - style: Style id from GET /text/styles.

- GET /api/v1/text/styles
  id: text.styles
  List every fancy text style

- GET /api/v1/text/zalgo
  id: text.zalgo
  Add combining characters (zalgo)
      - text (required): Text to stack.
      - mode: Direction of the marks.
      - amount: Marks per character.

- GET /api/v1/text/small-caps
  id: text.small-caps
  Convert text to small caps
      - text (required): Text to convert.

- GET /api/v1/text/spoiler
  id: text.spoiler
  Wrap text in Discord spoilers
      - text (required): Text to hide.
      - mode: line or char.

- GET /api/v1/text/divider
  id: text.divider
  Build a text divider
      - char: Character to repeat. Defaults to the first preset.
      - length: How many characters.

- GET /api/v1/text/status
  id: text.status
  Build a Discord custom status
      - text: Status text, up to 128 characters.
      - emoji: Optional leading emoji. Only added when it is missing.

- GET /api/v1/text/mentions
  id: text.mentions
  Build mention strings
      - type: Mention type id.
      - ids (required): IDs to wrap.

- GET /api/v1/text/mention-types
  id: text.mention-types
  List mention templates

- GET /api/v1/text/stats
  id: text.stats
  Word, character and reading stats
      - text (required): Text to measure.

- GET /api/v1/text/transform
  id: text.transform
  Case changes and stylisers
      - text (required): Text to transform.
      - mode (required): Transform to apply.

### IDs

- GET /api/v1/snowflake
  id: ids.snowflake
  Decode a snowflake
      - id (required): The snowflake to decode.

- GET /api/v1/snowflake/create
  id: ids.snowflake-create
  Build a snowflake from a date
      - date (required): ISO date or timestamp.
      - worker_id: Worker id, 0-31.
      - process_id: Process id, 0-31.
      - increment: Increment, 0-1023.

- GET /api/v1/ids/mock
  id: ids.mock
  Generate fake snowflakes
      - count: How many to generate.
      - kind: What the ids are for. Only changes the wording, never the format.

### Discord

- GET /api/v1/discord/users/:id
  id: ids.user
  Look up a user
      - id (required): User ID, or any string containing one.

- GET /api/v1/discord/guilds/:id
  id: ids.guild
  Look up a server
      - id (required): Guild ID, invite code or discord.gg link.

- GET /api/v1/discord/invites/:code
  id: ids.invite
  Look up an invite
      - code (required): Invite code or full discord.gg link.

- GET /api/v1/discord/emojis/:id
  id: ids.emoji
  Look up an emoji
      - id (required): Emoji ID.

- GET /api/v1/discord/snowflakes/:id
  id: ids.snowflake-exists
  Check whether a snowflake is a real user
      - id (required): Snowflake to check.

- GET /api/v1/badges
  id: dev.badges
  List every user badge

### Invites

- GET /api/v1/invites/extract
  id: invites.extract
  Pull the code out of an invite link
      - url (required): Any invite link or bare code.

- GET /api/v1/invites/images
  id: invites.images
  Resolve a server icon and banner from an invite
      - code (required): Invite code or full discord.gg link.
      - size: CDN size. 16 to 4096.

- GET /api/v1/invites/build
  id: invites.build
  Validate invite options and build the query string
      - channel_id (required): Channel the invite points at.
      - guild_id: Guild ID, for the invite payload.
      - max_age: Seconds before expiry.
      - max_uses: 0 is unlimited.
      - temporary: Members get the Temporary Membership flag.
      - unique: Force a new code.
      - target_type: 1 stream, 2 embedded application.
      - target_id: Target application or stream ID.

### Webhooks

- GET /api/v1/webhooks/payload
  id: webhooks.payload
  Build and validate a webhook payload
      - username: Webhook username override.
      - avatar_url: Webhook avatar override.
      - content: Message content.
      - include_content: Always include an empty content field.
      - thread_id: Send into a thread.
      - embed: Embed object: title, description, color, fields and so on.

- GET /api/v1/webhooks/limits
  id: webhooks.limits
  Embed and webhook limits

- GET /api/v1/webhooks/rpc
  id: webhooks.rpc
  Build a rich presence payload
      - text (required): Main text, what you are doing.
      - verb: Which activity type to use.
      - state: Optional second line.
      - started_at: Epoch milliseconds, for the elapsed clock.
      - large_image: Application icon key or URL.
      - small_image: Secondary icon key or URL.

### Permissions

- GET /api/v1/permissions
  id: permissions.compute
  Convert permission names to an integer, or back
      - permissions: Permission names, comma separated. Case and spacing do not matter.
      - integer: Decimal, 0x hex or 0b binary integer.

- GET /api/v1/permissions/all
  id: permissions.list
  Every permission with its bit

### Emoji

- GET /api/v1/emojis
  id: emoji.library
  Search the built-in emoji library
      - q: Match against name, character or keywords.
      - category: Category id.
      - limit: Maximum results, 1-500.

- GET /api/v1/emojis/categories
  id: emoji.categories
  List emoji categories

- GET /api/v1/emoji/color-text
  id: emoji.color-text
  Get coloured text, or find out why you cannot
      - text (required): Text to colour.
      - hex (required): Colour as a hex string.
      - mode: embed for the payload a bot posts, blocks for the decoration.

### Developer

- GET /api/v1/base64
  id: codecs.base64
  Base64 encode or decode
      - input (required): Value to convert.
      - mode: encode, decode, encodeUrl or decodeUrl.

- GET /api/v1/url
  id: codecs.url
  Percent-encode or decode a URL component
      - input (required): Value to convert.
      - mode: encode, decode or component.

- GET /api/v1/json
  id: dev.json
  Format, minify or validate JSON
      - input (required): JSON text.
      - mode: What to do with it.
      - indent: Spaces per level for pretty mode.
      - sort_keys: Sort object keys recursively.

- GET /api/v1/uuid
  id: dev.uuid
  Generate v4 UUIDs
      - count: How many, 1-100.

- GET /api/v1/color
  id: dev.color
  Convert a colour between every format
      - hex: Hex colour, with or without the #.
      - rgb: RGB string or object.
      - hsl: HSL string or object.

- GET /api/v1/password
  id: dev.password
  Generate a password and score it
      - length: Characters, 4-128.
      - uppercase: Include A-Z.
      - lowercase: Include a-z.
      - digits: Include 0-9.
      - symbols: Include punctuation.
      - avoid_ambiguous: Drop l, 1, I, O, 0 and similar.

- GET /api/v1/token/decode
  id: dev.token
  Read the structure of a token
      - token (required): A token you already own.

- GET /api/v1/timestamp
  id: dev.timestamp
  Convert a date to Discord timestamp formats
      - date: ISO date or timestamp. Defaults to now.

- GET /api/v1/message-links
  id: dev.message-link
  Split a message link into IDs
      - url (required): A discord.com message link.

- GET /api/v1/markdown
  id: dev.markdown
  Discord markdown reference

### Misc

- GET /api/v1/vtt
  id: misc.vtt
  Parse WebVTT captions
      - input (required): VTT file contents.

- GET /api/v1/age
  id: misc.age
  Age statistics for a date
      - dob (required): Date of birth, YYYY-MM-DD or ISO.
      - from: Reference date. Defaults to now.

- GET /api/v1/countdown
  id: misc.countdown
  Format seconds as a countdown
      - seconds (required): Total seconds.

- GET /api/v1/sounds
  id: misc.sounds
  List the synthesised soundboard

### Generators

- GET /api/v1/generate/usernames
  id: gen.username
  Generate usernames
      - style: Style id.
      - count: How many, 1-50.

- GET /api/v1/generate/nicknames
  id: gen.nickname
  Generate nicknames
      - count: How many, 1-50.

- GET /api/v1/generate/bio
  id: gen.bio
  Generate a bio
      - count: How many, 1-50.

- GET /api/v1/generate/server
  id: gen.server
  Generate a server name
      - channels: Channel names, 1-30.

- GET /api/v1/generate/channels
  id: gen.channel
  Generate channel names
      - count: How many, 1-50.

- GET /api/v1/generate/roles
  id: gen.role
  Generate role names
      - count: How many, 1-50.

- GET /api/v1/generate/rules
  id: gen.rules
  Assemble a rules template
      - titles (required): Template titles to include.
      - server_name: Substituted into the wording.

- GET /api/v1/generate/welcome
  id: gen.welcome
  Assemble a welcome message
      - server_name (required): Server name.
      - user_name: Name of the member being welcomed.
      - member_count: Member count shown in the message.
      - channel_name: Channel to point them at.
      - rules_url: Link to the rules.
      - style: embed, plain or image.
      - accent: Hex colour for the embed style.

# Documentation

## API

Source: https://distools.itzdanti.dev/docs/api

The API is the same code the tools run, exposed as an ES module and as JSON the browser can
render. It is served by GitHub Pages from this repository, so there is no separate backend to
deploy and nothing to sign up for. A process that wants a live HTTP API can run the server
included in the repository (`npm run serve`); GitHub Pages itself only serves files.

## What a static API means here

GitHub Pages serves files. There is no process behind the domain that can read a query string
and compute an answer. That shapes the whole design, so it is worth being straight about what
works and what does not.

  Pages can serve a file, so it answers endpoints that need no parameters. It has no process, so
  a **parameterised** call such as `?text=hello` cannot be answered there. The handler accepts
  `GET` with query parameters and `POST` with a JSON body; both work through the client module and
  against a self-hosted `npm run serve`, and neither works as a bare `fetch` or `curl` to Pages.

Three ways to call it, in order of how much you should care:

1. **Open the URL.** `distools.itzdanti.dev/api/v1/text/fancy?text=hello&style=bold` renders the
   JSON in your browser. Good for sharing and for eyeballing a response.
2. **Import the client.** `https://distools.itzdanti.dev/api/v1/client.js` is a dependency-free
   ES module that bundles the handler. **This is the supported way to call the API from code**,
   in a browser or in Node 18+.
3. **Pre-baked JSON.** The discovery documents are real files, so `curl` returns JSON with the
   right content type:

```bash
curl https://distools.itzdanti.dev/api/v1/openapi.json
curl https://distools.itzdanti.dev/api/v1/index.json
curl https://distools.itzdanti.dev/api/v1/health.json
curl https://distools.itzdanti.dev/api/v1/tools.json
```

A plain `fetch()` of a *parameterised* endpoint from another origin will not work, and it is
worth understanding why rather than assuming you did something wrong: Pages has no handler for
that path, so it returns the HTML shell. Import the client and it runs in your own runtime.

## Using the client

```js

// GET, with query parameters.
const fancy = await api.get("/text/fancy", { text: "hello", style: "bold" });
console.log(fancy.data.output);

// Array parameters repeat the key.
const counter = await api.get("/text/counter", { text: "ab", repeat: 3 });

// Errors carry the status and the payload the endpoint produced.
try {
  await api.get("/text/fancy", { style: "nonsense" });
} catch (error) {
  if (error instanceof ApiRequestError) console.log(error.status, error.message);
}

// The shareable URL for any call.
console.log(api.url("/text/fancy", { text: "hello" }));

// Look endpoints up to build a menu, or to check what a tool supports.
console.log(findEndpoint("/text/fancy").params);
```

It runs in Deno and in Node 18+ as well, since it has no DOM dependencies. Nothing it does
touches this site: the module is the logic, not a proxy.

## Response shape

A successful call returns the result under `data`, alongside enough context to log it:

```json
{
  "data": { "output": "𝗵𝗲𝗹𝗹𝗼" },
  "endpoint": "text.fancy",
  "method": "GET",
  "path": "/api/v1/text/fancy"
}
```

Errors look like this, with a matching HTTP status:

```json
{
  "error": { "message": "\"style\" must be one of: bold, italic, underline.", "status": 400 },
  "endpoint": "text.fancy"
}
```

## Conventions

- **Lists** are comma-separated, or repeat the key. `?items=a,b,c` and `?items=a&items=b` both
  work. Commas never separate on spaces, so names containing spaces survive.
- **Booleans** accept `1`, `true`, `yes` and `on`.
- **Numbers** are validated. An out-of-range value is a `400` with the range in the message,
  never a silent clamp.
- **Unknown paths** return `404` and point at the index.
- **Discord lookups** are the only endpoints that touch the network. Invites work. Guild and
  user routes answer `401` from Discord without a token; the endpoints pass that through with an
  explanation instead of hiding it.

## Contributing

Source: https://distools.itzdanti.dev/docs/contributing

Pull requests are welcome, including from people who have never contributed to anything before.
If you can open a pull request, you can contribute here.

## Getting set up

You need Node 20 or newer.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/itzdanti/distools.git
cd distools
npm install
npm run dev
```

That serves the site on `http://localhost:5173`. There is no backend to start and no environment
file to fill in.

## Adding a tool

A tool is three things: the logic, a registry entry, and a page.

**1. Write the logic in `src/lib/core/`.** Keep it a pure function that takes plain values and
returns a plain value. No React, no `document`, no `fetch` unless the tool genuinely needs the
network. This is what lets the same code power the page, the API endpoint and the API client.

```ts
// src/lib/core/shout.ts
export function shout(text: string): string {
  return `${text.toUpperCase()}!`;
}
```

**2. Register it in `src/tools/registry.tsx`.** Give it a stable slug, because slugs are URLs
and appear in the API. Add an icon, a category and a short description that says what it does
rather than what it is called.

**3. Build the page** in `src/tools/<category>.tsx`, using the shared `<Panel>`, `<Field>` and
`<Button>` components so it looks like the rest of the site.

## Adding an API endpoint

Endpoints live in `src/lib/core/api.ts` and are declared next to each other with a handler that
uses the same core module the tool uses.

```ts
{
  id: "text.shout",
  method: "POST",
  path: "/api/v1/text/shout",
  group: "Text",
  summary: "Uppercase text and add an exclamation mark.",
  description: "Takes text and returns it shouted.",
  tools: ["shout"],
  params: [{ name: "text", in: "body", type: "string", required: true, description: "..." }],
  handler: (input) => ({ output: shout(required(input, "text")) }),
}
```

A few rules that the tests will not catch for you:

- **Never accept a webhook URL.** Not in any endpoint, under any name.
- **Never accept a token.** There is no authenticated mode to put it in.
- **Use `required`, `int` and `oneOf`.** They produce the standard `400` shape, and they are what
  keeps invalid input from reaching your logic.
- **Pure functions only.** The same handler runs in a browser, in Node and in the pre-baked
  build step. If it reads the clock, pass the time in.

Once it is registered, the endpoint appears automatically in the per-tool API panel, in the
`/docs/api` reference, in `openapi.json` and in `dist/api/v1/index.json`. There is no list to
update by hand.

## Before you open the pull request

```bash
npm run lint         # oxlint, no errors
npm run test:config  # DISTOOLS_CONFIG still parses
npm run build        # type-checks and builds
npm run docs:openapi # regenerate openapi.json if you touched the API
npm run verify       # all of the above: lint, tests, build, dist and server checks
```

If you added an endpoint, add it to the smoke tests too. They run the real handler against real
input and check the error shapes, which is the part most likely to be wrong.

## Releases

Maintainers cut releases, not pull requests. A `v*` tag, or the **Deploy and release** workflow
run by hand, builds the site and publishes a GitHub release whose notes are the commits since the
last tag. You do not need to update `CHANGELOG.md`; it lists the project's shape, and the per-release
notes are generated from commits.

## House rules

- **Match the surrounding code.** Comments explain why, not what. Two-space indent, double
  quotes, semicolons.
- **Do not add a dependency without asking.** The bundle is small on purpose.
- **Do not add a network call to a tool that does not need one.** Pure tools stay pure, and the
  privacy page stays true.
- **Keep the copy human.** "Paste an invite link", not "Enter the invite identifier".

## Reporting a bug

Open an issue with what you did, what you expected and what happened instead. A screenshot
helps. If it only happens on one tool, say which one and which browser.

Security problems: open a private advisory on the repository rather than a public issue.

## Getting started

Source: https://distools.itzdanti.dev/docs/getting-started

Every tool is on one page and works the moment the page loads. There is nothing to install,
no sign-in, and no setting to configure.

## Tools that use the network

Most tools are pure computation: fancy text is string replacement, a snowflake decoder is
arithmetic, the permission calculator is bitwise maths. Those never touch the network.

A smaller group does make an outbound request, because the data lives on Discord's servers and
not in your browser. Those tools carry a **network** badge in the corner of their card.

The request contains only the thing you typed — a user ID, a guild ID, an invite code, or an
emoji ID. Nothing else from the page is attached.

## How a lookup is routed

  
    ### Your own API

    If the site is published with a hosted API configured, the lookup goes there first. Same
    origin, so no cross-origin question at all.
  
  
    ### Discord directly

    Otherwise the browser asks Discord itself. Most of the time this is blocked by Discord's
    CORS policy, but not always.
  
  
    ### A public proxy

    If the browser blocked that, the request is relayed through a public, unauthenticated CORS
    proxy. This works, and it is also the weakest link: the proxy can see the request. That is
    why nothing private should go into a lookup field.
  

The tool reports which route answered, so you always know whether a proxy saw your request.

## What Discord will and will not tell you

Worth knowing before you conclude a tool is broken:

- **Invites work.** `discord.gg/whatever` returns the server name, member count, online count
  and icon, with no token.
- **Servers by ID usually do not.** `GET /guilds/{id}` answers `401` to anonymous callers as of
  October 2026. Discord wants a bot token, and this site has none and will never ask you for one.
- **Users by ID are ambiguous.** `GET /users/{id}` also answers `401`, and deliberately does not
  say whether that means the account is private or does not exist. The tools report "no public
  profile" instead of guessing.
- **CDN images are public.** Avatars, banners, server icons and emoji can be embedded directly.

Where a route is restricted, the tool says so plainly rather than showing a spinner forever.

## Webhooks

A webhook URL is a password. Anyone holding it can post as that webhook.

The two webhook tools send **straight to Discord** from your browser. Nothing is relayed through
a proxy, and no endpoint in the API accepts a webhook URL at all. Delete the webhook when you
are done with it.

## Introduction

Source: https://distools.itzdanti.dev/docs/index

aki's Discord Tools is 57 small utilities for Discord servers and users. Fancy text, snowflake
decoding, permission maths, invite inspection, webhook sending, emoji work.

Everything runs in your browser. There is no account, no database and no server holding
anything you type.

## Privacy

Source: https://distools.itzdanti.dev/docs/privacy

The short version: there is nothing to sign up for, nothing is stored, and no tool on this site
will ask you for your password, your token or your 2FA code.

## What is stored

Nothing. There is no database, no account system and no analytics script. The site sets no
cookies. The only thing it will ever write to your browser is your theme preference, in
`localStorage`, and clearing site data removes it.

## What leaves your browser

Two categories of tool send anything at all.

**Lookups.** Tools that fetch a profile, avatar, banner or invite send the one identifier you
typed — a user ID, a guild ID, an invite code, an emoji ID — to Discord, or to a public CORS
proxy if Discord blocked the direct call. Nothing else from the page is attached. The tool tells
you which route answered, so you always know when a third party was involved.

**Webhooks.** The webhook tools post straight to Discord with the URL you pasted. A webhook URL
is a credential: anyone holding it can post as that webhook. Delete it when you are finished.

## What never leaves your browser

Everything else. Fancy text, snowflake decoding, timestamp conversion, the permission
calculator, colour shading, the token inspector, emoji resizing and image cropping are all
computation on data you already have. Open the network tab and watch.

## The token inspector

It decodes the *structure* of a token on your machine: which parts are present, roughly when it
was issued, what the flags say. It never transmits the token, and it cannot tell you whether a
token is valid, because that would require sending it.

A genuine Discord support agent will never ask for your password, your token or your 2FA code.
Nobody will.

## The API

The same rules apply, with two additions.

There is no authentication, because there is nothing to authenticate against. No endpoint
accepts a token, and **no endpoint accepts a webhook URL at all** — that is why the two webhook
senders have no API endpoint. If you find an endpoint that will take a webhook URL, it is not
this API.

The Discord endpoints are the only ones that make an outbound request, and they request exactly
one thing: the resource you asked for.

## Hosting

The site is a static bundle on GitHub Pages. GitHub serves the files and logs the requests in
the ordinary way any web host does. There is no application server, no database and no
third-party analytics embedded in the page.

## Terms of service

Source: https://distools.itzdanti.dev/docs/terms

By using aki's Discord Tools you agree to these terms. They are short because the service is
simple: it is a static site of browser-side utilities, offered as-is to anyone.

## What this service is

aki's Discord Tools is a collection of free utilities for Discord. Every tool runs in your
browser. There is no account, no server that processes your input, and no fee.

## Acceptable use

Use the tools only for lawful purposes and on data you are entitled to work with. In particular:

- Do not use the tools to harass, dox, or harm anyone.
- Do not use the webhook tools to send spam, malware, or content that violates Discord's own
  [Terms of Service](https://discord.com/terms) or [Community Guidelines](https://discord.com/guidelines).
- Do not attempt to use the site to attack, overload, or gain unauthorised access to any system.

You are responsible for the webhooks you interact with. A webhook URL is a credential: anyone who
has it can post as that webhook. Only use webhook tools on webhooks you own or are trusted to use.

## No warranty
